title: 016 · Why? #6: heads AND a six, chance? (why probabilities multiply; predict-first, white, synthwave)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Probability. Toss a coin, roll a die. Chance of heads AND a six? A 2/3 · B 1/12 · C 1/6 👇

Draw every outcome as a square: 2 coin columns × 6 die rows = 12 equal cells.
Heads takes half the square. A six takes one row. Both together is the one cell where they cross: 1 of 12 = ½ × ⅙ → B.
Add a second coin and that cell halves again: 1/24 = ½ × ½ × ⅙. Each "and" cuts the space, which is why we multiply.
Trap: adding (½ + ⅙ = ⅔) is for "or", and only multiply when one event doesn't change the other (independent events).
